summary:
Set 120 Session 3 (SET-TERMINAL) computes the session progress projection ONCE, carries the states absence used to hide, and removes the `<- here` marker under the operator's ruling.

(1) THE PROJECTION REUSES THE DERIVATION RATHER THAN SHIPPING A THIRD ONE. `ai_router/session_projection.py` serializes a session set's steps, states, what is in flight and what remains to `session-progress.json` beside the artifacts it derives from. It calls `session_checklist.build_rows` instead of reimplementing the reconciliation rule -- a set whose entire premise is 'the derivation exists twice' answering it with a third implementation would have been the joke writing itself. That makes 'computed once' STRUCTURAL: there is no second Python answer that could drift, and it makes the parity proof non-tautological, because the real check is that the SERIALIZED FILE reproduces the renderer, which is the property a later set needs before it can delete the TypeScript half. The read-side leniency is likewise DERIVED from `session_checklist.STATUS_BOXES` by box glyph rather than re-spelled as a second alias table, so the projection cannot recognise a token the renderer does not (L-069-1 -- the first cut of this module DID hardcode the alias map, and it was caught and fixed before any test ran).

(2) DERIVED AND REGENERABLE -- A CACHE, NEVER A SOURCE. Every file carries `derived: true`, the exact regenerate command, and the SHA-256 of each input (activity-log.json, session-state.json, spec.md), so `projection_state()` always answers fresh / stale / absent / unreadable, `--check` exits 3 on anything but fresh, and a `schemaVersion` newer than the reading code reads as unreadable rather than being guessed at. An input that APPEARS or VANISHES is a change like any other, so the digest maps are compared key-set first. `close_session` regenerates it after flipping the state snapshot, declared through the Set 119 S3 CLOSE_MANDATED_WRITES mechanism rather than by adding a filename to a list in verification_stamp -- so a close-time write cannot stale the verification stamp it is written after. The declaration must be an `ast.literal_eval`-able literal: the first cut referenced the module constant and FAILED CLOSED, which is the mechanism working as designed, and a test now pins the literal against the constant.

(3) THE STATES ABSENCE USED TO HIDE -- AND A FOURTH THE SPEC DID NOT NAME. `unknown` for a status token no reader can name, which is where 11 of the 15 entries Session 2 deliberately preserved now surface, raw token intact rather than laundered (the projection carries BOTH `status` and `state` precisely so the entries protected from laundering stay protected). `unreadable` beside `absent` and `read` for the ledger itself, so 'no work' and 'cannot read the evidence' stop being the same empty session row -- a defect both Set 115 reviewers named independently. `stale` for the projection against its own inputs. AND `orphanEntries`: measuring found that Session 2's other 4 preserved entries (Set 028's absent-`status` population, flagged as S3's headline case) reach no reader at all, because they carry no `sessionNumber` and `build_rows` drops them in BOTH languages. Reported as a top-level COUNT and not as rows, deliberately: inventing rows for entries that name no session would put the projection at odds with the renderer it must reproduce, and the parity proof would have been the thing that broke.

(4) THE `<- here` MARKER IS GONE (operator ruling, 2026-08-11). HERE_MARKER, both rendering sites, `_mark_here` and `ChecklistRow.is_here` are removed, and `record_post` now records `inProgressStepKeys` -- a list, always present, possibly empty -- instead of the hereStepKey/hereStepNumber/hereStatus triple. The marker inferred a single current row and that inference is what pointed confidently at step 1 of Set 119 S2 while the real work was four steps on; since Set 120 S1 the `in-progress` token carries the fact directly, and because the fact is per-row, two steps may now be in flight at once. Removing it from Python without touching `tools/` was the session's one real design tension: `is_here` is a field the SHARED Python/TypeScript parity corpus pins in all 34 of its expected rows. Resolved and journaled -- the corpus's `cases` stay byte-identical, the Python half compares the five fields both implementations still produce, and the divergence is declared in the corpus's `_readme`. Two new guards keep that honest: SHARED_ROW_FIELDS is asserted against ChecklistRow's own dataclass fields so a new field cannot silently stop being compared, and a second test REFUSES a cleanup that strips `isHere` from the corpus, because that field is now the only coverage the extension's marker has.

Verification: VERIFIED on both discovery lenses, 0 blocking findings, 4 nits -- two accepted and fixed, one taken as a named residual owned by the extension carve, one dismissed on measurement.

notes.test_run_of_record: pytest: 3,871 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed in 538.06s (8:58), run on the frozen tree AFTER the last code change and recorded in test-runs.jsonl (digest aa828265a873, 539s). notes.stamp_staleness_is_expected: Round 1 was stamped, then the two accepted nits were fixed. Both are documentation-only, but freshness is computed over the tree, so `close_preflight` correctly reported the round-1 stamp as stale. The choice was: leave known-stale prose I had just introduced (worse, and contrary to L-065-1 and L-064-8, which that very round had cited), or re-verify. Re-verified, before the close rather than inside it -- which is what close_preflight's COST line advises, and it keeps the round inside the machine-enforced bound of 2 discovery passes.
notes.suite_falsification: Three mutations, one per shipped property, each confirming the suite is not vacuous (L-112-1). Healing an unknown token to `complete` fails test_an_unnameable_token_projects_as_unknown_without_being_healed. Disabling staleness detection fails test_a_touched_input_makes_the_projection_stale. Re-inserting the literal `<- here` into `render` fails test_no_rendered_surface_carries_a_here_marker -- the one that matters most, because deleting a constant is invisible if something writes the string back, so that falsifier asserts on rendered TEXT rather than on the absence of a name.
notes.pre_existing_test_tightened: `test_the_guidance_files_are_never_wholly_exempt` asserted `close_mandated_excludes(...) == []` while its docstring claimed to be about the two guidance files. That proxy held only while cite_lessons was the sole declaring module, and it failed the moment a legitimately whole-file artifact was declared. It now asserts what it says it asserts -- that neither guidance path is wholly exempt -- which is both stricter about its actual claim and correct under the change. The test was tightened, not deleted or weakened.
notes.test_budget: 6 net test functions (7 new in test_session_projection.py, 2 new in test_step_row_parity.py, 3 marker tests removed from test_session_checklist.py), against the 7 the set had left. SET TOTAL: 39 of the spec's 40-function irony budget. Measured per file from the staged diff, not estimated.
decisions_this_session: How to remove the here-marker without touching tools/ (authority=ai, rubric_line=goal-over-letter, verification_effect=none). The shared parity corpus pins `isHere` in all 34 expected rows and sessionStepModel.test.ts deepStrictEquals against it, so removing ChecklistRow.is_here forced a choice. CHOSEN: keep the corpus's `cases` byte-identical, narrow only the Python comparison, declare the divergence in the corpus's `_readme` (data the TypeScript suite never asserts on). Recorded as verification_effect=none deliberately: dropping an assertion normally reduces verification, but `isHere` ceases to EXIST on the Python side, so the assertion has no subject rather than a weakened one -- and the gate still proves the whole reconciliation rule it was built for.

Where the projection lives, and whether it recomputes (authority=ai, rubric_line=simpler-code, verification_effect=none). The spec's Touches line named ai_router/progress.py, but that module is the set-level session-state normalizer and touches no activity log. CHOSEN: a new module that DELEGATES to session_checklist.build_rows. Surfaced rather than done silently, because it departs from the spec's stated Touches list.
spec_departures_reported: The spec's Touches line for Session 3 names `ai_router/progress.py`. It was not touched; the projection went to a new `ai_router/session_projection.py`. Journaled with the reasoning rather than quietly substituted.

Step 3's list of absence states is `unknown` / `stale` / `unreadable`. A fourth was found by measurement (`orphanEntries`) and shipped, because it is the same defect class and it is where Session 2's remaining 4 preserved entries had gone. Reported here rather than folded in silently.
notes.lessons_note: L-069-1 and L-065-1 were both instrumental this session -- the derived alias table instead of a second one, the named tools/ residual, and the propagation of the marker removal to every prose echo -- but they are NOT listed in lessons_cited and cite_lessons was NOT run for them. Both have been PROMOTED: their canonical rules live in project-guidance.md, which is loaded at every session start, so the citation signal that drives archival decisions is moot for them. The operator confirmed this for L-069-1 explicitly at session start ('promoted from lessons-learned to project-guidance; there is no need to reactivate it'), and L-065-1 is the same case. The four cited ids are the active-tier lessons that were genuinely instrumental.
notes.step_9_review: Reorganization review of project-guidance.md / lessons-learned.md: NO CHANGES RECOMMENDED. The preload sits at 11,856 of its 12,000-token ceiling (99%), and every individual file is at 98-100% of its own, so any addition is an eviction decision. One candidate lesson was considered and REJECTED against the Set 085 admission test: 'a test that asserts a proxy broader than its own docstring fails on a correct change' (the test_the_guidance_files_are_never_wholly_exempt case). It has one instance, not a recent recurrence, and its miss cost is low -- the test fails loudly rather than hiding a defect -- so it fails admission on two of the five criteria. It is recorded in this disposition and in the changelog instead, which is where a one-instance observation belongs. No promotion is owed either: the lessons that carried this set (L-069-1, L-065-1) are already promoted, which is why they did not need citing.
owed_residuals: The extension still computes `isHere` (sessionStepModel.ts:328) and renders HERE_MARKER (workExplorerTreeModel.ts:660), and its comments still describe markHere as mirroring the now-deleted session_checklist._mark_here. Owner: the extension carve. The shared corpus deliberately still pins the TypeScript behaviour, and a test refuses any cleanup that strips it.

Nothing CONSUMES the projection yet. It is written at close and checkable with `--check`; the Work Explorer still derives its own rows. That is standing decision 3 working as intended, not an omission -- but until the carve lands, `session-progress.json` is a produced artifact with no reader.

The absent-`status` four (Set 028) are still an open WRITER decision, named by S1 and inherited by S2 and S3. This session made them visible (`orphanEntries`) rather than deciding whether absence should be refused at the writer. Whoever takes it should note the four entries carry no `sessionNumber` either, so they are malformed in more than one way.

The UAT-matrix fixture's 2 `completed` tokens remain unmigrated by Session 2's journaled decision (pinned test data, not a record of a real session). A future set that carves the extension can migrate them in the same pass that owns its tests.

`skipped` remains refused by the writer. Session 3 makes re-admitting it substantially cheaper -- after the carve it is a one-place change instead of a two-language one -- but it stays a decision, not a consequence.

The repo-wide line-ending normalization was deliberately NOT attempted inside a close. .gitattributes now covers the stamped verification artifacts only; every other file still round-trips through core.autocrlf=true. A future set should decide whether * text=auto eol=lf is wanted repo-wide, and if so must do it as a dedicated pass -- the working-tree copies of historical artifacts are CRLF today, so a careless --renormalize would commit that translation into the record rather than out of it.
notes.next_set_recommendation: The extension carve (target-state proposal 6.5) is the natural successor and this set exists to unblock it. `session-progress.json` is the one computed answer it was waiting on, so that set can delete sessionStepModel.ts (~1,830 lines), its ~110 tests, ai_router/tests/test_step_row_parity.py and the shared parity corpus in the same pass that teaches the Work Explorer to read the projection -- and in doing so it clears three of the five residuals above at once. Set 115 Session 4 is also unblocked (it was blocked because it would have rendered corrupt data), but whether it is re-authored or dropped remains its own decision and should not be assumed.
notes.manual_verification: Operator authorized manual verification for this close on 2026-08-11 to wrap the set up. Verification was NOT skipped: it ran TWICE, cross-provider, and passed both times -- round 1 VERIFIED on both discovery lenses with 4 nits, round 2 VERIFIED on both lenses with 0 findings against the committed tree. The stamped rows stopped validating mechanically for two BOOKKEEPING reasons, neither of which changed a reviewed byte: (1) the rebase onto origin/master to pick up an unrelated operator commit moved the evidence base away from 998abdcbe0a2, so round 1s work_diff no longer matches the tree diffed from the base it recorded; and (2) core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes let that rebase rewrite round 1s RAW ARTIFACTS from LF to CRLF (775->780 and 491->495 bytes, no character changed), breaking their stamped artifact_sha256. Attestation text: s3-manual-verify-attestation.txt. Nothing else the close gates on is bypassed by the flag.
notes.line_ending_defect: FOUND AND FIXED THIS SESSION, and worth a future sets attention. The constitution says a verification artifact is a raw record and is NEVER edited after it is written -- but core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes meant GIT ITSELF edited two of them, silently, on an ordinary rebase, and that is sufficient to invalidate stamped evidence repo-wide. A targeted .gitattributes now marks the stamped artifacts (s*-verification*.md, s*-issues*.json, path-aware-critique.json) as binary so translation is off in both directions, and the two corrupted artifacts were restored to their exact committed bytes from the git blob -- a restoration, not an edit. A git add --renormalize docs/session-sets was attempted and IMMEDIATELY REVERTED: with the new binary marks it would have stored the CRLF working-tree copies of ~100 historical sets artifacts, rewriting the raw records of every prior verification round in the repo. That is the opposite of the invariant being defended, and it is recorded here because the near miss is the useful part.
